components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Committed action with Quiet Olive emphasis and a calm physical press state.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 44px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-md, 0.5rem); background: var(--primary, oklch(0.355 0.06 125)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.985 0.006 83)); padding: 0.625rem 1rem; font: 500 0.875rem/1.25 Avenir, sans-serif; transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), background-color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.96); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--background), 0 0 0 5px var(--foreground); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action that stays within the Linen surface hierarchy.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { min-height: 44px; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.87 0.015 75)); border-radius: var(--radius-md, 0.5rem); background: var(--background, oklch(0.982 0.009 83)); color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.195 0.015 55)); padding: 0.625rem 1rem; font: 500 0.875rem/1.25 Avenir, sans-serif; transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), background-color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--muted, oklch(0.948 0.012 80)); } .ds-btn-outline:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.96); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--background), 0 0 0 5px var(--foreground); }

narrative.overview: DespreSine should feel like entering a private room prepared for attention: warm but unsentimental, quiet without becoming vacant, and composed without appearing institutional. Linen surfaces provide calm ambient light; Quiet Olive marks action, focus, and living detail; black-brown ink keeps the experience serious and legible. The system is editorial in rhythm and restrained in interface behavior.
keyCharacteristics: Linen-first surfaces with rare, purposeful Quiet Olive emphasis.
Avenir across display, body, and controls, differentiated by scale and rhythm.
Generous editorial spacing and readable line lengths.
Rounded, lightly outlined surfaces with flat resting states.
Botanical light and photography used as atmosphere, not proof or decoration.
Brief, compositor-safe motion with reduced-motion equivalents.

rules.name: The Rare Olive Rule
rules.body: Quiet Olive is a semantic accent, not a decorative wash. Its scarcity preserves calm and makes actions easier to recognize.

rules.name: The Linen Continuity Rule
rules.body: Adjacent sections separate primarily through space, content, and tonal layering; full-width divider lines are exceptional.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Use the incumbent Avenir stack for public interface and editorial roles. Create contrast through scale, spacing, and occasional italic emphasis rather than introducing another font.

rules.name: The Breathing-Room Rule
rules.body: Preserve section space before adding borders, shadows, decorative bands, or additional containers. Empty space is structural.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: A static surface should not look lifted unless it must float over media or another interactive layer. Hover and open states may introduce subtle elevation to confirm response.

dos: Do use Linen as the dominant surface and Quiet Olive for rare semantic emphasis.
Do create hierarchy with scale, line length, space, and copy before adding decorative containers.
Do use approved professional photography and botanical light sparingly.
Do keep public interactions keyboard-accessible, responsive, and complete under reduced-motion and reduced-transparency preferences.
Do make privacy and non-diagnostic limits visible at sensitive decisions.
donts: Don't introduce bright palettes, therapy clichés, clinical-dashboard styling, generic wellness imagery, or marketplace trust patterns.
Don't use Quiet Olive as a broad decorative background or color every interactive element.
Don't add a second public type family without replacing this documented system through an explicit design decision.
Don't stack borders, shadows, and nested rounded containers when spacing or tonal layering communicates the relationship.
Don't use motion as spectacle or allow it to obscure content and controls.
